title: Elasticsearch Search & Analytics
description: Production Elasticsearch reference covering documents, mappings, analyzers, indexing, Query DSL, relevance, aggregations, vector and hybrid search, shards, replicas, data streams, lifecycle, ingest pipelines, security, capacity, snapshots, upgrades, and troubleshooting.

subtopics.title: Indices, Shards, Segments & Documents
subtopics.description: An index is split into primary shards with replicas. Each shard is a Lucene index composed of immutable segments; refresh makes changes searchable while flush/commit and translog support durability.

diagram.content:
flowchart TD
  Index["Logical index / data stream"] --> P0["Primary shard 0"]
  Index --> P1["Primary shard 1"]
  P0 --> R0["Replica shard 0"]
  P1 --> R1["Replica shard 1"]
  P0 --> S0["Lucene segments"]

callouts.title: Near Real Time Is Not Immediate Search
callouts.text: A successful index response does not guarantee a normal search sees the document before refresh. Use refresh deliberately; forcing it per write harms throughput.

subtopics.title: Mappings, Field Types & Dynamic Fields
subtopics.description: Map fields by query/aggregation behavior. text is analyzed for full-text search, keyword preserves exact values, and numeric/date/geo/vector types enable specialized operations.

rows: Using object arrays when pair association matters

callouts.title: Mapping Explosion Is an Outage Risk
callouts.text: Unbounded user-defined keys create fields and cluster-state pressure. Use explicit templates, flattened structures where suitable, and total-field/depth limits.

subtopics.title: Analysis, Ingest Pipelines & Bulk Indexing
subtopics.description: Analyzers tokenize and normalize text at index/search time. Ingest pipelines transform documents before indexing; bulk requests improve throughput but require per-item error handling.

callouts.title: Bulk HTTP Success Can Contain Item Failures
callouts.text: Inspect every item, retry only retryable failures with backoff, preserve IDs/idempotency, and bound request bytes and concurrent bulk workers.

subtopics.title: Query DSL: Query vs Filter Context
subtopics.description: Query context calculates relevance; filter context answers yes/no and is cache-friendly where appropriate. Compose bool clauses for must, filter, should, and must_not.

callouts.title: Avoid query_string for Raw User Input
callouts.text: Its syntax can be surprising and expensive. Prefer structured Query DSL or simple_query_string with explicit fields and limits.

subtopics.title: Relevance, Sorting & Pagination
subtopics.description: BM25-style scoring depends on analyzed terms and corpus statistics. Tune with representative judgments; use deterministic sorts and search_after with point-in-time for deep consistent pagination.

callouts.title: from/size Deep Pagination Is Expensive
callouts.text: Each shard must collect enough earlier hits. Bound pages, use search_after/PIT for traversal, and use asynchronous export patterns for bulk extraction.

subtopics.title: Aggregations, Vector & Hybrid Search
subtopics.description: Aggregations summarize buckets and metrics; vector search retrieves semantic neighbors; hybrid retrieval combines lexical and semantic evidence with explicit fusion or reranking.

codeBlocks.code:
Lexical: analyzed terms, phrase/proximity, synonyms, exact filters
Vector: embedding model + dimensions + similarity + k/candidate budget
Hybrid: retrieve both → fuse/rerank → apply authorization filters
Evaluate: labeled queries, recall, precision/NDCG, latency and cost

callouts.title: Embeddings Are Versioned Data
callouts.text: Record model, dimensions, normalization, source text, and generation time. Model changes usually require controlled reindexing and relevance comparison.

subtopics.title: Cluster State, Node Roles & Allocation
subtopics.description: The elected master manages cluster state; data nodes hold shards; allocation balances constraints and tiers. Availability requires master quorum and shard copies across failure domains.

callouts.title: Yellow and Red Mean Different Risks
callouts.text: Yellow means primaries assigned but replicas missing; red means at least one primary unavailable. Diagnose allocation instead of blindly changing watermarks or replica counts.

subtopics.title: Shard Sizing, Routing & Hot Spots
subtopics.description: Shard count affects parallelism, recovery, heap, cluster state, and overhead. Route documents evenly unless deliberate locality outweighs hot-key and availability risks.

codeBlocks.code:
Estimate: daily indexed bytes × retention × replica factor
Benchmark: representative mappings, queries, aggregations, refresh and merge load
Observe: shard size/count, segment count, heap, search/index latency, recovery time
Change: rollover, shrink/split/reindex according to lifecycle—not guesswork

callouts.title: More Shards Is Not Automatically More Scale
callouts.text: Oversharding consumes heap and CPU and slows recovery; oversized shards lengthen movement and failure recovery. Benchmark and set operational targets.

subtopics.title: Data Streams, Lifecycle, Aliases & Reindexing
subtopics.description: Data streams manage append-oriented time-series backing indices. Lifecycle policies roll over, tier, downsample, retain, or delete; aliases enable compatible index migrations.

codeBlocks.code:
Template + mappings + lifecycle policy
→ data stream/write alias
→ rollover by size/age/docs
→ warm/cold/frozen or downsample where justified
→ delete after retention
Mapping/analyzer break → create new index → reindex → validate → atomically switch alias

callouts.title: Reindex Needs Source-of-Truth and Cutover Design
callouts.text: Handle concurrent writes, version conflicts, throttling, validation, aliases, rollback, and additional storage. Elasticsearch may be a derived index rather than the authoritative store.

subtopics.title: TLS, Authentication & Authorization
subtopics.description: Use TLS for transport and HTTP, scoped API keys or supported identity realms, least-privilege index/application permissions, field/document controls where required, and protected administrative access.

codeBlocks.code:
Application identity → API key with exact index privileges
Human identity → SSO realm + role mapping
Network → private endpoints, TLS, no public anonymous cluster
Sensitive settings → Elasticsearch keystore / managed secret service
Audit → auth failures, privilege changes, sensitive searches/admin actions

callouts.title: Never Expose Elasticsearch Directly to Browsers
callouts.text: Place an application boundary in front to validate queries, enforce tenant/object authorization, limit cost, redact errors, and protect credentials.

subtopics.title: Snapshots, Restore & Upgrades
subtopics.description: Snapshots are incremental repository backups of cluster data/state according to selected scope. Register protected repositories, automate policies, test restores, and follow supported rolling/full-restart upgrade paths.

callouts.title: Filesystem Copies Are Not Supported Backups
callouts.text: Copying node data directories cannot produce a consistent cluster backup. Use snapshot APIs and verify feature state, security configuration, repository access, and application recovery.

subtopics.title: Diagnostics & Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Correlate workload with cluster health, JVM pressure, disk watermarks, thread-pool rejections, shard allocation, slow logs, tasks, circuit breakers, and client retry behavior.

callouts.title: Production Checklist
callouts.text: Design mappings explicitly, bound fields and bulk/query cost, test relevance, size shards from benchmarks, use lifecycle policies, spread replicas, secure every endpoint, snapshot and restore, monitor JVM/disk/rejections, avoid retry storms, and rehearse reindexing and upgrades.
